objective: Encode consecutive UTF-16 code-unit runs with one indexed for loop and literal decimal counts.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: String indexing and run counting remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Run counting is a practical small parsing exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: UTF-16 versus code-point boundaries are transferable.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The explicit encoding contract prevents an ambiguous character definition.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Distinguishing encoding from reversible compression avoids a false guarantee.

defects: Character meant code unit in every supplied program without saying so.
Senior used an additional while loop despite the requested single for.
No bound or stated cost model covered string accumulation; digits make this delimiter-free encoding ambiguous to decode.
rationale: Define literal UTF-16 code-unit runs, whitespace/digit preservation and 10000-unit bound; this is encoding without an unambiguous decoder guarantee. Replace senior with a one-pass indexed counter. Use a conservative quadratic portable concatenation bound rather than claiming engine-independent full-prefix copying. Test paired/lone surrogates by numeric output code units, avoiding transport of lone surrogates; newline/tab expression inputs use escaped literals. Add 10000 identical and alternating units. An intermediate malformed test expression caused hidden-check errors and was replaced before final evidence.

objective: Find the smallest-first integer pair with inward-moving while-loop pointers without writing to input.

relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Linear pair search is a common interview and data-processing exercise.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Monotone movement and duplicate indices transfer widely.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded integer arithmetic makes exact equality and pointer reasoning clear.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Read-only ownership and a deterministic tie policy prevent subtle errors.

defects: Junior used quadratic nested loops and senior used for rather than the requested while.
Number domain and successful-result freshness were implicit.
No fresh repeated-result assertion or upper-bound pair existed.
rationale: Use inward while pointers in all boards; bounded integer values/targets avoid floating-point equality ambiguity. Preserve duplicate-at-distinct-index matches and smallest first value. Add repeated-result freshness, multiple valid pairs, frozen bounded arrays, 10000-item terminal match/no-match, and a read-only array Proxy that records/refuses writes. An in-place sort on an already sorted array produced no observable writes in this runtime, so that unsuitable negative candidate was removed from both selected baseline/final summaries; its original baseline remains privately retained. The final batch has 34 selected verdicts, with nine wrong candidates. Either zero sign is accepted.

objective: Scan each full positive-sized window with nested indexed for loops and return original finite maxima.

relevanceRationale.transferable: Initializing from an actual value avoids negative-input bugs.

relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Bounds and nonmutation make the exercise predictable.

defects: Senior used Array.from, slice and spread Math.max instead of the required nested for loops.
Zero/noninteger sizes and nonfinite inputs were unspecified.
No ownership/freshness, no-rounding or bound cases existed.
rationale: Keep the clear nested scan and align senior to it. State size 1..1000, at most 1000 finite values, read-only ownership, no rounding and fresh results. Either zero sign is valid. Explain quadratic worst-case versus tighter windows-times-width cost. Add negative fractional values, signed zeros, repeated empty/fresh results and 1000 items with width 1/500/1000.

Object cloning and width truncation passed old cases.
rationale: Align both boards with the requested nested loop order. Define 0..100 dimensions, dense rectangular frozen/read-only outer and rows, opaque element identity and new output rows on every call. Zero rows or zero width returns fresh empty output. Add mixed opaque/undefined/NaN/signed-zero values, cross-call and row/input nonaliasing, zero-width input and 100×100 corner positions.
